name: Ultramontanism
summary: Ultramontanism is the nineteenth-century Catholic current that centred authority in the papacy, opposing Gallicanism and state control of the Church. It rejected liberalism, the separation of church and state and secular schooling, as set out in Pius IX's Syllabus of Errors, and backed the pope's infallibility defined at Vatican I. It is a church-political doctrine with little economic programme.
scope: The mainstream ultramontane movement of the nineteenth century, from de Maistre's Du Pape through Pius IX, the Syllabus of Errors (1864), Louis Veuillot and Manning, to Vatican I (1870). It does not cover later Catholic social teaching or post-Vatican II views. Many economic and modern issues are inferred and low confidence.

furtherReading.title: The Syllabus of Errors
furtherReading.note: The papal text that best expresses the ultramontane stance on liberalism and the state.

keyFigures.name: Joseph de Maistre
keyFigures.role: Author of Du Pape (1819), the leading theoretical defence of papal sovereignty.

sources.title: Ultramontanism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, opposition to Gallicanism and regalism, Vatican I, later history.

sources.title: Ultramontanism
sources.author: Umberto Benigni, The Catholic Encyclopedia (1912)
sources.usedFor: Church liberty from the state, opposition to the secular post-Revolution state, Centre party.

sources.title: The Syllabus of Errors (1864)
sources.author: Pope Pius IX
sources.usedFor: Condemned propositions on church-state separation, religious freedom, education, marriage, socialism.

sources.title: Joseph de Maistre
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Counter-revolutionary monarchism, authority from religion, critique of rationalism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The movement was about church authority and anti-liberalism; nineteenth-century ultramontanes left health provision to charity and the Church, and later Catholic social teaching is split on state roles.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Ultramontanism took no stand on wage law; a just-wage idea appears only in later papal social teaching, which the sources do not tie to the movement.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement condemned liberalism, which included economic liberalism, but it had no economic programme; inferred from its hostility to liberal individualism.

public-ownership.rationale: The Syllabus condemns socialism and communism, so state ownership of industry would be rejected, though ultramontanes did not defend laissez-faire either.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The movement was not concerned with taxation; adherents' views followed their social class and country.

unions-good.rationale: Ultramontanism predates Catholic labour doctrine; adherents distrusted secret societies but later favoured Catholic-run associations, so they are split.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Syllabus defends the Church's own property and condemns socialism, implying support for property rights; inferred, as property was not the movement's focus.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No ultramontane position on corporate regulation is documented; the movement's concern was ecclesiastical authority.

cut-welfare.rationale: The movement left poor relief to the Church and charity but defended no cut-welfare doctrine; adherents are split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialist schemes are condemned in the Syllabus; worker ownership of firms was foreign to ultramontane thought, so it is inferred as disagreement.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The issue is anachronistic; ultramontanes favoured strong authority but also complained of state intrusion on the Church.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's moral conservatism and view that law should uphold Catholic morality.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Ultramontanes demanded Church censorship of error but not 'hate speech' protections; they would condemn attacks on religion while resisting modern speech codes.

strong-leader.rationale: Ultramontanes want a strong papacy and, with de Maistre, sovereign authority, but a leader bypassing gridlock in a secular state is not their concern.

state-harmful.rationale: Ultramontanes held that civil authority is legitimate and divinely ordained; the movement defended order, not abolition of the state.

limit-guns.rationale: The issue is anachronistic and not tied to the movement.

empower-police-military.rationale: Counter-revolutionary thinkers like de Maistre prized order and authority, so more state force against revolution is inferred as agreeable.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Ultramontanes demanded that law uphold Catholic morality and condemned liberal moral permissiveness; legalised prostitution would be rejected.

decide-locally.rationale: The movement centralised authority in Rome against national and local church autonomy; for civil matters it sought no localism, though it also resisted state centralism.

rehabilitation.rationale: De Maistre defended harsh punishment, yet Catholic tradition also values reform of the sinner; adherents are split.

traditional-family.rationale: The Syllabus defends indissoluble sacramental marriage and Church jurisdiction over it, making the traditional family central to the Catholic order ultramontanes defended.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic, but the Syllabus insists marriage is a sacrament governed by Church law; same-sex marriage would be firmly rejected.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not discussed in the Syllabus, but it is inferred from ultramontane fidelity to Catholic doctrine, which condemns abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Ultramontanism is integral Catholicism opposed to the secular state; it wants the Church's role in public life strengthened.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the movement's concerns.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from Catholic natural-law anthropology that ultramontanes defended against modernism.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ultramontanes put the universal Church above national churches and distrusted nationalism, though they defended Catholic customs in places like Quebec and Spain; split.

gradual-change.rationale: Ultramontanes respected established institutions and the Church, but in the Syllabus they rejected accommodation with modernity and sought reversal of liberal reforms.

reduce-immigration.rationale: No ultramontane position is documented; a universal Church is not hostile to migrants, yet conservatives were wary.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The UN is anachronistic; ultramontanes did want a supranational spiritual authority in the papacy but not secular world government.

free-trade.rationale: Economic policy was not part of the movement.

nation-first.rationale: Ultramontanes were accused of being loyal to a foreign power because they placed the universal Church above national interest.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's preference for ordered, hierarchical society.

limit-growth.rationale: Anachronistic; ultramontanes were not degrowth thinkers though they criticised materialism.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic and unrelated to the movement.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The Syllabus rejects the claim that the Pope should reconcile with progress and modern civilisation; faith in progress was a liberal error.

revolution-justified.rationale: De Maistre blamed the French Revolution on rationalism, and ultramontanes opposed revolution as a rule; the Syllabus also rejects the lawfulness of rebellion.

experts-over-public.rationale: Ultramontanes favoured authority of the hierarchy over popular opinion in the Church, but not technocracy.

central-planning.rationale: Socialism is condemned in the Syllabus; centrally planned economies are inferred as rejected.

socialized-markets.rationale: Socialist models are condemned and the economy was not a movement concern; inferred disagreement.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of property and family against socialism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy never entered ultramontane writing, which dealt with church authority rather than economic planning.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Later Catholic social teaching favours widely held property but this is not documented for the nineteenth-century movement.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolition of wage labour is a socialist aim, and the Syllabus condemns socialism and communism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions were not an ultramontane concern, and the sources record no stance on them.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Some Catholic corporatists later drew on the tradition, yet the ultramontane movement itself did not define the position; split.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Centre party was called the Ultramontane party, showing the movement worked through party politics; rule by a single ideological party is not its model.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: De Maistre defended divine-right monarchy and the Bourbon restoration, though ultramontanism itself accepted several regimes.

democracy-best.rationale: De Maistre rejected rationalist popular sovereignty, and Pius IX condemned liberal popular-sovereignty theories; democracy was not treated as best.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from the hostility of de Maistre and the Church to popular sovereignty.

workers-councils.rationale: A socialist form of power rejected with socialism and communism.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; regional separation was not a movement issue.

natural-rulers.rationale: De Maistre held that sovereignty is divinely ordered and not made by the governed, and the movement held the hierarchy rules the Church by divine right.

political-violence-never.rationale: Ultramontanes did not renounce force, as de Maistre defended the executioner and states' coercion, but they opposed revolutionary violence; split leaning to disagree.

war-builds-character.rationale: De Maistre wrote of war as providential, but the movement did not teach this and the papacy preached peace.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Syllabus (section 55) condemns the proposition that Church and State should be separated.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Ultramontanes wanted Church teaching to guide law, but through natural law and papal authority, not scripture alone.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from the movement's view that authority rests on divinely sanctioned sovereigns.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement stressed a universal Church over national or ethnic bases.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist class-conflict theory is part of the socialism the Syllabus condemns; ultramontanes saw providence and the Church as driving history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Egalitarian levelling is inferred as rejected with socialism and the hierarchical outlook.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land claims lie outside the movement's nineteenth-century debates over papal and state authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations for colonialism were not discussed by ultramontane writers, so there is no documented position.

civilizational-union.rationale: The movement wanted Catholic unity under the pope, but not a political union of civilisations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The movement condemned liberal individualism; self-interest as a moral good is contrary to Catholic ethics.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Syllabus denies that individuals have a right to profess any religion, and stresses obedience to authority and duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy was not part of the movement, and no ultramontane source takes a side.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from Catholic teaching on marriage and family.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Counter-revolutionaries lamented modernity's moral effects but did not call industry a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Rejects reconciliation with progress and modern civilisation, so speeding disruption is disfavoured.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Catholic teaching on human nature.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's rationale for authority was divine, not technical.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is a modern issue with no connection to the church-state disputes that defined ultramontanism.

restore-past-order.rationale: De Maistre and the ultramontanes wanted to undo the Revolution and restore Christian social order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement held that doctrine and Church authority, not pragmatic results, decide, and it condemned liberal accommodation.

direct-action.rationale: Ultramontanes organised through party politics, as with the Centre party, and the Church.

means-match-ends.rationale: The movement's sources give no view on whether methods must mirror the intended society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No ultramontane support; inferred from its civilised hierarchical Christian order.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A radical communist aim, so rejected with communism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist distribution is condemned, but Christian charity stresses care for the needy; split.

production-for-use.rationale: Ultramontanes wrote on authority and doctrine, not on the purpose of production, so adherents have no common line here.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Marxist theory of exploitation belongs to the socialism condemned in the Syllabus.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Syllabus condemns socialism and communism, and ultramontanes defended hierarchy and order. The dictatorship-of-the-proletariat formula is later, so the source does not address it as such.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation is a communist policy and rejected.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Marxist theory is rejected with Marxism; ultramontanes blamed secular liberalism instead.

taxation-theft.rationale: Ultramontanes held that legitimate authority rests on divine sanction, so taxation by such authority is not theft.

harm-principle.rationale: The Syllabus rejects liberal freedom of conscience and worship, and the state may enforce Catholic morality.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement defended the corporate rights of the Church against the state and rejected the individualism of liberal rights.

conscription.rationale: Ultramontane sources are silent on military service; adherents could accept it under legitimate rulers.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hierarchical idea of authority.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of the secular utilitarian state.

positive-liberty.rationale: The distinction between positive and negative freedom was not part of ultramontane debate, so no stance is documented.

media-academia-power.rationale: The Catholic Encyclopedia describes a coalition of rationalists and others opposed to the Church; its stance is hostile to secular press and universities, though power claims are inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not part of ultramontane teaching; Catholic doctrine held human unity.

organic-representation.rationale: Some Catholic traditionalists favoured corporate representation, but the movement is not documented on it.

total-state.rationale: Ultramontanes defended the Church's independence from state control and opposed state direction of education and culture.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ultramontanes sought restoration of Christian order rather than a national palingenesis, and the sources record no position.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not part of the movement's aims; it defended the papal states, not conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths of personal loyalty are not discussed in the movement's sources, though loyalty to the pope was central in Church matters.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Ultramontanes held that truth is objective and held by the Church, not constructed by power, though they argued that secular teaching served error.

universal-morality.rationale: The movement defended Catholic natural-law teaching as binding truth for all, against relativism condemned in the Syllabus.

single-common-good.rationale: Ultramontanes thought politics should serve a single Catholic order of truth rather than balance interests, an inference from integral Catholicism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora citizenship rights were not an ultramontane topic, so no position is documented.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; Latin and Roman unity were more important.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from rejection of socialism and of democratic principles.

school-vouchers.rationale: Ultramontanes demanded Church control of schooling and opposed state monopoly (Syllabus sections 45-47), which public funding of Church schools would serve.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy was outside the movement's concerns and the sources record no position.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic liberalism was not a movement doctrine and liberalism was condemned.

rule-by-example.rationale: De Maistre stressed authority sanctioned by religion and punishment alongside example; split.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement defended the Papal States and Church supremacy over nationalism, so it did not accept self-determination as a general right.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN postdates the movement, which had no doctrine on authorising force beyond just-war teaching.

reason-over-faith.rationale: De Maistre held that rationalist justification of authority undermines it, and the Syllabus condemns rationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare entitlements for immigrants were not an ultramontane issue; the Church ran charity itself.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work requirements for welfare were not discussed by ultramontanes, who left relief largely to Church charity.

class-collaboration.rationale: Opposed to class conflict and socialism; the Catholic view is of harmony between orders, though the movement did not elaborate it.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement was about conserving inherited institutions and rejected the break with tradition.

dominated-front.rationale: A common front of Western-dominated countries has no counterpart in ultramontane thought.

workers-nation.rationale: The question of whether workers organise nationally or internationally is a socialist debate absent from ultramontane writing.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Syllabus's defence of traditional marriage and family implies distinct roles; the movement did not legislate on it.

ban-interest.rationale: Canon law once condemned usury, but nineteenth-century Catholics had accepted lending; split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not a movement position; Catholic doctrine affirms common humanity.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist claim rejected in the Syllabus's condemnation of socialism; ultramontanes saw authority as divinely based.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is a modern matter on which ultramontane sources are silent.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigrant assimilation was not a theme of the movement, which stressed a universal Church over national culture.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems were not a concern of the movement, which was suspicious of popular sovereignty itself.

national-mission.rationale: The movement saw the Church, not a nation, as having a universal mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred; the movement affirmed traditional hierarchy and would not call it injustice.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Ultramontanes attacked liberal and anticlerical politicians but did not frame the political class as corrupt in general.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic coercion contradicts Catholic teaching on marriage and the person.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Legal accountability for past state killings is a modern transitional-justice question with no ultramontane position.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement wanted the state to uphold Catholic religion and morals, not be a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contrary to Catholic teaching on marriage; not a movement position.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Catholic doctrine of equal souls applies, but the Syllabus rejects liberal legal equality of religions, so confidence is low.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism as a category is modern and was not addressed by ultramontane writers.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Syllabus rejects civil jurisdiction over marriage and subordination of Church law, which a uniform civil code would imply.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Ultramontanes wanted Catholic establishment and Protestant proselytism restrained (section 77 on religion of the state), but not a general conversion law; split.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Syllabus (sections 45-47) condemns state control of schools free of Church authority.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Ultramontanes and de Maistre located legitimacy in divine sanction, not in popular consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade goals were outside the ultramontane agenda, and no source gives a position.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Ultramontane thinkers like de Maistre accepted state coercion and war as providential, so an absolute ban on initiating force is not theirs; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist ideas conflict with Catholic ethics and with the Syllabus's rejection of unchecked progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Ultramontanes were themselves targeted by bans during the Kulturkampf and would object to such powers in anticlerical hands.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican theory of freedom was not part of ultramontane debates, so no position is documented.

separated-powers.rationale: Ultramontanes favoured a Church independent of state, a type of dual authority, but did not endorse constitutional separation of powers in general.

vanguard-party.rationale: A communist doctrine, condemned with communism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Charity was central to Catholicism but the movement did not make it a legal priority.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is a twentieth-century British policy outside the movement's period.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law was not debated in ultramontane sources, and adherents had no shared view.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred from Catholic opposition to Malthusian ideas.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ultramontane writing treated religious unity, not ethnic diversity, as the basis of cohesion, so no direct position is documented.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred from the movement's view that authority is divinely sanctioned, not random.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Counter-revolutionary thought valued order, but the movement was not documented on emergency powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls on food were not a topic for the movement, and adherents had no common view.

party-controls-media.rationale: Ultramontanes opposed state control of the press as an attack on Church independence, though they sought Church censorship of error.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of armed forces is alien to the movement.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation periods were not an ultramontane concern.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for legislators was not discussed by the movement, so no position is recorded.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Centre party worked as a bloc under the Church, but the principle is not defined in the sources.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational unions such as the EU postdate the movement, which only sought a universal spiritual authority in the papacy.

head-commands-forces.rationale: De Maistre favoured strong monarchy, but no explicit view on this.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Ultramontanes held that the Church is governed by its hierarchy under the pope, not by congregations or assemblies. The statement's "national church" framing fits poorly, since they opposed national churches run by their own bishops (Gallicanism).

clerical-rule.rationale: Ultramontanes claimed papal authority over spiritual and some civil affairs, but in practice defended Church liberty rather than rule by clergy; split.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist doctrine; revolutionary defeatism contradicts counter-revolutionary politics.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Syllabus and the movement supported Church censorship of error and condemned the claim that free expression doesn't harm morals (section 79).

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits for presidents were not part of the movement's concerns.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from rejection of popular-sovereignty institutions.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances were not discussed in ultramontane sources, so there is no documented position.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred; property was defended against socialism.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred from the movement's order and authority emphasis.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Counter-revolutionary Catholic writers contrasted rural piety with urban secularism, but this is inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The movement's territorial concern was the Papal States, not reunification of divided nations in general.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Ultramontanes opposed secular universities, but the claim as stated is not documented.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The movement held Catholic Christendom to be the true civilisation and the Syllabus rejects equality of religions.

death-penalty.rationale: De Maistre defended capital punishment and the executioner's role in the social order, and the Papal States used it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The Syllabus rejects state control of schooling and moral teaching apart from the Church.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Syllabus resists secular science overriding Church teaching (section 12), but the movement did not demand creationism; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The movement wanted law to support Catholic morals and condemned the claim that unrestricted expression is harmless (section 79).

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The rules for passing citizenship were not an ultramontane topic.

minority-language-support.rationale: Minority language policy is not discussed in the sources, though Latin liturgy was prized.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Ultramontanes defended the Church's liberty from state interference and sought exemptions for Catholics, e.g. in the Kulturkampf, though minority protection generally was not their theme.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style individual liberty is the liberalism condemned in the Syllabus.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third-world debt cancellation is a modern issue that ultramontanism never addressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: This anti-colonial claim has no counterpart in the movement's concerns.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Popular constitution-making conflicts with the Syllabus's rejection of popular sovereignty.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Developmentalist trade-offs of freedom for growth were not addressed by the movement.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Charity is a Catholic duty, but the movement's sources set out no doctrine of international aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement, so no position is documented.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from preference for monarchy and divine legitimacy.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking policy was not part of the ultramontane agenda.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Ultramontanes defended the pope's territories (the Papal States) against surrender, which supports this as a principle.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Catholic doctrine holds property has a social function, but nineteenth-century ultramontanes stressed property rights against socialism; low confidence.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The debate over the nature of the Soviet Union postdates the movement.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation doctrine is modern and unaddressed in ultramontane sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance guarantees such as NATO's postdate the movement, and no stance is documented.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The movement viewed the annexation of the Papal States as unlawful, but a general principle is not set out.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Syllabus condemns placing the clergy under civil authority and state control of Church property and rights (for example sections 19, 24, 41-42).

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ultramontane sources do not discuss the ceremonial role of a head of state, though it fits papal ideas of a ruler above faction.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Ultramontane writing does not address secession, though it defended the Papal States against annexation.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special autonomy arrangements for regions were not addressed by the movement.

sacred-ruler.rationale: De Maistre saw sovereignty as divinely sanctioned, though not as divine descent; Catholic doctrine rejects ruler divinity.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax structure was outside the movement's concerns.

character-from-environment.rationale: The movement affirmed original sin and moral nature, not environmental determinism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: De Maistre saw sovereigns as bound by divine law and the pope's authority over rulers; the Church's claim of papal supremacy limits rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration postdates the movement, and no stance is documented.

mixed-constitution.rationale: De Maistre favoured monarchy but acknowledged mixed forms like Britain's; not a defining view.

leader-cult.rationale: The papal cult of personality arose within Church, but civil leader worship contradicts Catholic teaching; split in practice.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody rules after separation are a modern matter, and divorce itself was condemned by the movement.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist idea outside ultramontane thought; rejected with Marxism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Seizure of estates is socialist-style expropriation, and the Syllabus defends property and Church holdings.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights were not an ultramontane topic.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Syllabus defends Catholicism as the state religion, but nineteenth-century ultramontanes did not uniformly seek legal penalties for apostasy; they were split.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union was not discussed by the movement, so no position is documented.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The movement valued a universal Church over ethnic unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural autonomy within states was not a theme of ultramontane writing.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Debates over minority emigration versus integration were not part of the movement's discourse.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: De Maistre and the ultramontanes saw religion, ideas and providence as the forces of history and blamed the Revolution on rationalism. This is inferred from their outlook; they did not address the materialist thesis directly.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy was not addressed by ultramontane writers.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts of banks or firms were not an ultramontane topic.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Ultramontanes rejected majority sovereignty as supreme and held a higher divine law binds states.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from traditional views of roles.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic bloc economics were absent from the movement's concerns.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding trade standards are a modern policy and no ultramontane source addresses them.

moral-incentives.rationale: The movement made no statement about replacing material incentives, though Catholic moral teaching values duty.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Revolution is the evil the movement opposed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: De Maistre defended hereditary monarchy and aristocracy and ultramontanes sided with the old order.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Ultramontanes saw Catholic Christendom as the centre of civilization, so history told from a Catholic or Christian standpoint is inferred as preferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from Catholic missionary work and the counter-revolutionary view of hierarchy and tutelage by the faithful over the unenlightened; not stated in the sources.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Syllabus rejects state control of schooling, so state-led civic loyalty teaching is inferred as disfavoured against Church-led education.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement was about church authority and gave no position on race-conscious admissions or hiring.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from opposition to expansion of state power over society and the older Catholic suspicion of finance; not addressed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The movement gave no teaching on capitalism's cycles; it condemned both socialism and liberalism, so adherents are split.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not an ultramontane concern; the focus was papal authority, not imperial legacies.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from hostility to liberal economic doctrine and attachment to a traditional order; no source states a position.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The Syllabus condemns socialism and Communism, so a class analysis of exploiter and exploited nations is inferred as rejected.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the view that property and conscience are subject to moral law taught by the Church, not unlimited private will.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Syllabus condemns liberty of conscience, worship and the press as rights, and holds that law should conform to Church teaching, not a secular charter.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: A nineteenth-century church-political movement that did not address colonial treaties; inferred neutral.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Syllabus condemns the idea that authority is only the sum of numbers, and de Maistre defended hereditary monarchy under papal moral authority.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on central authority over local or dissenting claims.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Syllabus condemns the proposition that it is lawful to rebel against legitimate princes.

parliament-supreme.rationale: De Maistre's counter-revolutionary monarchism and the Syllabus reject parliamentary sovereignty.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from Catholic moral teaching against cruelty; not a defining issue.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from Catholic tradition that permits use of animals with limits against cruelty.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from Catholic charity and the Church's traditional duty toward the poor.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ultramontanes organised politically, for example the Centre party, to defend church liberty, so they rejected withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; ultramontanes distrusted the liberal press but did not hold this theory.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: a Marxist-derived claim opposed to the movement's view of legitimate authority.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Syllabus condemns socialism; the dependency thesis is inferred rejected.

party-own-road.rationale: The Syllabus condemns socialism and communism, but the statement concerns inter-party autonomy, which is not addressed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from Pius IX's refusal to accept the loss of the Papal States, the Roman Question.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hierarchical view of authority; not addressed.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from its traditionalism and reverence for inherited religious and historical symbols.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Syllabus condemns the claim that the Church should be reconciled with progress and modern civilization, implying one true order rather than plural forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; the movement focused on the Church, not the army.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the Syllabus defence of traditional family and marriage under religious law.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred: Catholic teaching on the fourth commandment, and de Maistre's stress on authority and hierarchy, imply strong filial duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: ultramontane thought favours offices by hierarchy and divine authority rather than examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: No stated position; ultramontane writings concern church authority, not the ownership of firms, so adherents have no distinctive view.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Syllabus of Errors condemns civil divorce and the claim that marriage is a purely civil contract.

recallable-delegates.rationale: De Maistre and the Syllabus reject popular sovereignty and the subjection of authority to the will of the governed.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Syllabus condemns socialism and communism and defends the right to property, so common land tenure is rejected.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: it rejected liberal constitutionalism but had no stated position on legislative budgets.

single-official-language.rationale: No stated position; the Church's own use of Latin and national languages was not an ultramontane issue.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred: a universal-church outlook with state-sanctioned Catholic orders leans against rights for outsiders, though no source states it.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: it opposed egalitarian doctrines and modern liberalism, and the Syllabus nowhere supports outcome-based tests.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred: the Syllabus condemns modern progress and civilisation (error 80), implying distrust of materialism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: No stated position; Papal Zouaves defended the papal states but no doctrine on arming foreign rebels.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred: Catholic powers intervened to defend the pope, but it has no stated doctrine on intra-bloc intervention.

corporate-influence.rationale: A church-political doctrine with no economic programme; its critique of liberal capitalism is not framed around lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Ultramontanes wanted the Church free of state control but nothing concerns funding of NGOs; no clear position.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Catholic teaching favours large families and the movement would back support for them; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: No stated view; ultramontanes were concerned with the Church's property, not residency rules.

job-guarantee.rationale: Poor relief was left to Church charity, but the movement had no stated position on state employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Syllabus rejects liberalism and progress and de Maistre distrusted democracy, so a democracy-spreads-peace claim is rejected; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Ultramontanes stressed obedience to legitimate authority, though not to unjust law; inferred from de Maistre's view of authority.

non-intervention.rationale: The Syllabus of Errors condemns as error 62 the proposition that "the principle of non-intervention, as it is called, ought to be proclaimed and observed", so ultramontanes reject a ban on intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; no stated position on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Ultramontane writers often blamed Freemasons and Jews for liberal revolution, but the movement was not defined by it and views varied; inferred as split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Syllabus condemns civil marriage and state control of marriage, upholding the Church's authority over it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: De Maistre defended mystery and hierarchy of authority, so a public right of access to state information is not a theme; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Ultramontanism was hierarchical, centred on the pope and bishops, not on small informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Ultramontanes placed loyalty to Rome above national churches and state control, so they resisted national supremacy over supranational authority.

religious-nation.rationale: The Syllabus condemns the separation of church and state and holds that Catholicism should be the state religion, so the nation is tied to the faith.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Ultramontanism centred on papal authority over the Church, not on tribute between states; the movement was indifferent on this.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The movement took no stand on regional revenue; inferred as indifferent.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Syllabus of Errors condemns socialism and communism, which includes common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Syllabus condemns communism along with socialism and secret societies as pernicious errors, though it says nothing of a state policy to defeat it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The Syllabus rejects state monopoly of education and defends church-run schools, so independent providers inside a public system fit; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Ultramontanism holds revealed religion to be true and necessary, and the Syllabus condemns rationalism and indifferentism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Ultramontanes opposed liberalism and the modern order; its economic form is inferred as rejected, not praised.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Syllabus defends the traditional family and Church teaching; economic transformation for women's equality is inferred as rejected.

socialized-care.rationale: The Syllabus defends the family and condemns socialism; ultramontanes left care to families and Church charity.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The movement held Latin as the Church's language but had no programme to purge loanwords; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Concordats between Church and state were central ultramontane instruments and were held binding; inferred as applying by analogy.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Ultramontanism defended the hierarchical Church and traditional social order; self-governing communal property is inferred as rejected.

majority-settlement.rationale: Church unity under Rome, not majority-group settlement, was the ultramontane concern; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Syllabus condemns both liberalism and socialism/communism, leaving authority and the Church as the sound basis.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the defence of the Papal States, which rested on historical and religious ties to Rome.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its loyalty to Catholic moral teaching and the historical record.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from Catholic moral teaching, which treated such acts as grave sin and, in the period, a matter for civil law.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Syllabus condemns liberty of the press and of opinion, which points toward restricting opposition, but ultramontanes themselves organised Catholic parties and associations, so this is inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Syllabus condemns the end of Catholicism as the sole state religion and the right of immigrants to public worship of their own (77-78), so the state may restrict the open practice of other religions. It says nothing about punishing blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The current set no line on colonies; inferred that adherents' views varied with missions and national interests.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: it would see resistance as a duty of defending Christendom, not of Muslims.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Mixed: de Maistre and the Church backed legitimate rulers and order, though the papal tradition allowed deposing rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from de Maistre's view of hierarchy and authority over popular decision-making.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its hierarchical, anti-liberal outlook.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Catholic teaching that sex is given by God.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from Catholic teaching on the sanctity of life.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: the Syllabus rejects liberalism and progress as the measure; the divide is Church against the modern world.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: it condemned socialism and liberal economics alike and did not use the concept of alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from its picture of Europe as Christendom.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: De Maistre and the Syllabus hold that authority comes from God through the Church, not from popular sovereignty.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The Syllabus rejects the separation of church and state and secular state schooling; religious symbols belong in state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; the current does not address it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not addressed; it condemned socialism and liberalism, with no settled view on regulated markets.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: the Papal States relied on armed defence of papal sovereignty.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its hierarchical but charitable outlook.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; the papacy claimed spiritual independence from all powers but its politics varied.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Ultramontanes favoured legitimate hereditary monarchy as in de Maistre's thought, inferred from his counter-revolutionary defence of throne and altar.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Ultramontanes were hostile to liberal finance but the Church condemned socialism; user-owned banks are not addressed, so inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The IMF is anachronistic; the movement had no position on lenders, so inferred as split.

property-franchise.rationale: The Syllabus rejects liberal democracy and de Maistre defended hierarchy, which fits a limited franchise, but no source addresses the vote, so the answer is inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ultramontanes held a hierarchical view of nature and the sexes, and the idea is a modern one; inferred disagree.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept foreign to the movement, which condemned socialism; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Ultramontanes valued a Catholic press and condemned liberal press freedom as licence, so wealth-owned presses were not their concern; inferred as split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: De Maistre and the Church favoured rule under law and tradition, though sovereign decree was accepted in the Papal States; a mild agree inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement was universal in the Catholic Church and not racial, but also favoured Catholic establishment; a racial franchise is not part of it.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement has no position.

open-government-data.rationale: Ultramontanes condemned liberal publicity and favoured authority and the Church's secrecy, so inferred mild disagreement.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Church opposed mixed marriages and the Syllabus insists on canon law over civil marriage; legal restriction fits ultramontane church-state views.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Catholic teaching condemns hatred of persons and the movement's goal was Church authority, not boycotts; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: ultramontanes upheld hierarchical authority and condemned popular sovereignty, so lot-chosen citizens deciding major questions runs against it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Syllabus of Errors condemns the idea that doctrine should be reconciled with progress and modern civilization, and ultramontanes insisted on fixed papal teaching.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Ultramontanism was a church-political doctrine with no economic programme; adherents were split between conservative defenders of property and later social-Catholic critics of capital.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed in the period; inferred from the movement's defence of traditional Catholic moral teaching on sexuality, which opposes public normalisation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Syllabus of Errors condemns state-run secular schooling and hostility to religion, and ultramontanes upheld the Church's claim over education.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from the ultramontane emphasis on divinely sanctioned authority and order, which leaves no room for abolishing coercive state institutions.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; ultramontanes sought Church privileges in confessional states rather than a view on consociational government, so adherents have no settled position.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the Church's claim that charity and education belong to the Church rather than the secular state, which ultramontanes defended against liberal state expansion.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; the movement concerned papal authority, not the tenure of elected politicians.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of popular sovereignty and liberal democratic innovation in the Syllabus and de Maistre; the question itself was never raised.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement had no view on extinction risk, which an adherent would likely subordinate to salvation and the Church's mission.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Ultramontanes upheld the all-male Catholic priesthood and hierarchy under the pope, with no admission of women to teaching or governing offices.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from nineteenth-century Catholic teaching on the husband as head of the family, which ultramontanes upheld against civil-marriage reforms.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Ultramontanes held a hierarchical, confessional view of the political community; extending local votes to foreign residents is inferred as unsupported.

rent-control.rationale: Nineteenth-century ultramontanism had no stated line on rent law; later Catholic social teaching is outside the scope.

abolish-ip.rationale: No stated position on patents and copyright; the Syllabus does not address it.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Ultramontanism had papal Zouaves but no mass youth-drilling programme; the issue is not addressed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Pius IX's temporal power depended on a French garrison in Rome, yet ultramontanes stressed the Church's independence from states; no stable line.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The question is anachronistic and adherents have no stated position.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Nineteenth-century ultramontanism had no economic programme; the Syllabus opposes socialism but is silent on this claim.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Catholic moral tradition has long allowed killing in lawful self-defence, so absolute pacifism is inferred as strongly rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Ultramontanism centred loyalty on the universal Church and the pope over national churches, so nation-centred continuity is inferred as secondary.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Traditional Catholic teaching treats sex as given by nature; inferred and anachronistic.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The anachronistic claim runs against the fixed natural order ultramontanes defended; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Ultramontanes honoured martyrs of the faith, which the pope canonises, rather than the nation's dead as saints; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Syllabus and de Maistre frame the modern revolutionary and liberal order as an error opposed to the Church, so politics is inferred as in part a spiritual struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred as not addressed; ultramontanism was universal, not a national homeland doctrine.

culture-before-state.rationale: Ultramontanes sought Church independence and papal authority first, not a national culture or state; no clear lead.

god-not-male.rationale: Ultramontane tradition used the traditional masculine language for God; the issue is anachronistic and inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Ultramontanes judged tradition by papal authority, not by a standard of women's full humanity; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Church was universal and overrode national distinctions; ownership by national majorities is inferred as not its doctrine.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: ultramontanism focused on Church governance and the Papal States, not merging regions by people.

independent-unions.rationale: Nineteenth-century ultramontanes favoured Catholic workers' associations but the movement had no settled view on union independence.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Syllabus of Errors condemns socialism and communism, so a socialist test of working-class power is rejected.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The movement was about church authority; it left health and charity largely to the Church, and views on local public services are inferred as split.

second-chamber.rationale: Ultramontanism was a church-political doctrine with no settled view on legislative design.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the Syllabus's defence of private property against socialism and from its distrust of secular communes.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the ultramontane emphasis on centralised authority under the pope and opposition to national or local autonomy of the Church.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from Catholic teaching on the family and the male provider; later papal social teaching adopted a family wage, but the nineteenth-century movement did not state it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement took no position on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement took no position on life-extension research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement took no position on financial privacy.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement took no position on digital identity.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the Syllabus's rejection of state omnipotence and of Hegelian state absolutism, though it also subordinated individuals to the Church.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Syllabus rejects materialism and naturalism and holds that the Church's spiritual end is higher than any temporal one.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The movement was about the Church against the state, not regional autonomy within states.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement took no position on agricultural biotechnology.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement took no position on urban form.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from the universal Catholic claim that the Church embraces all peoples, which sits badly with organising by race.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred as split; the universal Church stressed religious rather than racial identity, but Catholic nationalist strands valued ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred as split; the papacy invoked just-war doctrine and defended the Papal States militarily, with no fixed defensive-only rule.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Ultramontanism put the universal Church above nation and state; inferred from its transnational papal loyalty, which subordinates national identity.

communal-electorates.rationale: Church-centred doctrine favoured confessional communities and church-recognised bodies; inferred from the Syllabus's rejection of the neutral secular state.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Ultramontanes saw hostile liberal and masonic forces rather than foreign partition plots; inferred and split.

free-public-college.rationale: Ultramontanes wanted education under the Church rather than a state system; the Syllabus condemns state control of schools, and free tuition is inferred to be unwelcome.

pollution-taxes.rationale: No ultramontane position; the anti-liberal, agrarian outlook gave no support to modern pollution taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Conservative, tradition-minded outlook implies duty to hand on inheritance; inferred and anachronistic.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Ultramontanes held traditional gender roles but also valorised Marian piety and women's religious orders; inferred and mixed.

arms-reduction.rationale: The papacy condemned war in principle but the movement backed Papal States defence; inferred, mixed.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Papal diplomacy was conducted through concordats and was confidential; inferred, no stated position.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; inferred as neutral.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the support for ordered authority and the papacy's own claim to sovereignty; no source addresses private arms directly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on obedience to lawful authority and Catholic just-war teaching, which does not endorse individual refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Mid-nineteenth-century ultramontanes had no settled position on bargaining; later Catholic social teaching, outside the scope, favoured unions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: No nineteenth-century position on tax credits; inferred as indifferent.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Nineteenth-century ultramontanism had no stated view on borrowing rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; adherents focused on church liberty rather than the global economic order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Ultramontanes were counter-revolutionaries who defended established authority; the Syllabus condemns revolution and de Maistre defends throne and altar.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from its claim that one divinely founded church and social order, not experiment, should shape society.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic to the nineteenth-century movement; no stated position.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred from its supranational loyalty to the pope and the Syllabus's condemnation of making the state or nation the highest authority.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from its defence of property and the Syllabus's hostility to socialism; student debt was not an issue.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed by ultramontanes; the claim is a modern one.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from Catholic teaching that human dignity rests on a created nature; the Syllabus condemns naturalism but does not speak to redesigning it.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the demand that the church and not the state control education and opinion, and its opposition to the secular state.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Syllabus condemns indifferentism and the view that men may find salvation in any religion (section III, propositions 15-18).

farm-price-support.rationale: Ultramontanism has no farm programme; rural paternalism was common but unspecific; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Maistre defended sovereign force and war as part of the providential order, so adherents would accept keeping arms; anachronistic, inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Syllabus condemns socialism and communism, so class-based workers' parties would be opposed; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Catholic natural-law teaching protects bodily integrity, so adherents would back a ban; anachronistic, inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Syllabus defends church and family law but does not address women's inheritance; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Ultramontanism has no position on language naming; inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: No position on pollution law; anachronistic.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Maistre defended inherited authority and intermediate traditional bodies as bulwarks of order; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The Syllabus condemns unlimited liberty but environmental protection is anachronistic; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Maistre defended severe, certain punishment as necessary to order; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Ultramontanism did not address immigrant language; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not addressed; the movement fought for church liberty rather than labour law, and Catholic corporatists favoured guilds, so this is inferred as split.

voter-id.rationale: Franchise rules were not a concern of the movement; Catholic parties like the Centre used the vote, and no stance is documented, so this is inferred as neutral.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Syllabus of Errors condemns religious equality and the separation of church and state, holding that Catholicism should be the state religion with legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Syllabus rejects popular sovereignty and the idea that the state is the source of rights, so rulers were legitimate through submission to church and tradition, not competitive elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Syllabus condemns civil marriage and defends Catholic marriage law, and church teaching holds sex outside marriage sinful.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the Syllabus condemning freedom of the press and from the movement's preference for order and authority over liberal freedoms.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's counter-revolutionary hierarchy and charity-based approach to the poor, which sits badly with a state cash-transfer scheme.

women-suffrage.rationale: Anachronistic; nineteenth-century ultramontanes assumed a hierarchical order of family and state with male public authority, though the Church later accepted women's voting.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Ultramontanes defended the Church as the guardian of morality and family, and would reject the claim that religion is a major cause of oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's universal Catholic mission is neither clearly for nor against this claim, so it is inferred as neutral.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of traditional family and male headship and its hostility to modern state social programmes.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Syllabus's defence of private property against socialism; first claim is not discussed.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the Syllabus's rejection of secular state supremacy and its claim that the papacy judges rulers; secular criminal courts are anachronistic.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Vatican I affirmed inspiration of scripture, but Catholics read it under church interpretation, not by plain literal sense; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the Syllabus's traditional view of family and church order; the question is anachronistic.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The Syllabus of Errors condemns socialism and communism, so a planned state would not be defended.

indirect-election.rationale: No stated position; the papacy chose by cardinals but ultramontanes favoured hierarchical authority over any particular electoral scheme.

national-church-status.rationale: The Syllabus condemns equality of religions and holds that the Catholic religion should be the state religion, though ultramontanes stressed the Church's liberty from state control.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was universalist and centred on Rome, with no stated stance on ethnic autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from Pius IX's rejection of the plebiscite annexation of the Papal States; the Syllabus denies that popular will confers legitimacy.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; the question is anachronistic.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the Christian ideal of restraint and the Syllabus's rejection of modern progress; not a stated position.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's silence; it favoured Catholic mission and settlement and did not address indigenous homelands.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the traditional gender roles in the Syllabus's view of family; the question is anachronistic.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Ultramontanes stressed Catholic tradition and the Papal States as a sacred patrimony, so a sacred duty to ancestral land is inferred, though the doctrine was supranational.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Catholic moral teaching of the period held that punishment required lawful process, and nothing in ultramontane sources supports killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: The doctrine never addressed China policy; it is inferred as indifferent, with only an interest in missionary access.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Ultramontanism defended Catholics as a church community across borders rather than a nation's kin; inferred as split between that and national loyalties.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Syllabus's defence of property and its condemnation of socialism; the Church also taught the universal destination of goods, so confidence is low.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Syllabus's rejection of liberal individual autonomy and claims of absolute personal right, in favour of duties under divine law.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The movement had no tax programme; the answer is a neutral inference.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Ultramontanes left poor relief to Church charity and had no view on state spending design; inferred as neutral.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Ultramontanes built party and press organisations such as the Centre party and defended intermediate bodies, so bypassing them is inferred as disagreed.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The doctrine did not address business privileges; inferred as neutral.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Syllabus condemns separating church from state and the Centre party organised Catholics politically, so ultramontanes rejected non-denominational politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Syllabus condemns reconciling with 'progress, liberalism and modern civilization' as then understood, yet ultramontanes used railways and the press; inferred mild agreement with technology under tradition.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Syllabus condemns propositions allowing civil divorce and holds marriage indissoluble, so unilateral divorce by a wife is rejected.

national-resource-control.rationale: Ultramontanism had no resource policy and was supranational; inferred as neutral.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The Syllabus defends private property against socialism, so a fortune honestly gained would be seen as legitimate; the process-versus-outcome question itself is inferred from that.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; nothing in the sources bears on taxing financial trades.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Nineteenth-century ultramontanes did not discuss racial disadvantage in these terms; no position can be sourced.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Syllabus (errors 56-59) condemns the claims that morals need no divine sanction and that right is only material fact, in line with the Thomist view that a law against justice lacks binding force.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not addressed; the movement had no view on automation and later Catholic teaching values both work and its limits.

multipolar-world.rationale: The movement sought papal spiritual authority over the whole Church rather than a balance of powers; inferred as split.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The Syllabus condemns socialism and communism, whose Marxist form rests on this theory; the theory itself is inferred as rejected.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The sources tie the movement to church authority, not to worker politics; patriotism was secondary to loyalty to Rome.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was about church authority and has no view on what the left should prioritise.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The Syllabus of Errors (section IV) condemns socialism and communism, so a communist-led system of any kind would be rejected.

missingStatements.text: The pope should have the final authority in matters of faith and morals for the whole Church.
missingStatements.rationale: Papal primacy and infallibility, defined at Vatican I, are the defining ultramontane claim, opposed by Gallicans.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to papal doctrine of the Catholic Church; too narrow for a question many ideologies take sides on, and church-governance stances are covered by church-by-bishops and clerical-rule.

missingStatements.text: Civil rulers should have no authority over the internal governance of a church.
missingStatements.rationale: Ultramontanes opposed Gallicanism, Josephinism and regalism by insisting on the Church's independence from the state.

missingStatements.text: Marriage should be governed by religious law rather than by the civil courts.
missingStatements.rationale: The Syllabus condemns the propositions that civil contract suffices for marriage and that matrimonial cases belong to civil tribunals (sections 73-74).

notes: Ultramontanism is a church-political movement; economic and modern issues are mostly inferred, so many answers are low or neutral. Some statements are repeated in the answer source only once.
